title: FlexCare: Leveraging Cross-Task Synergy for Flexible Multimodal Healthcare Prediction

problem.claim: Multimodal healthcare prediction must handle correlations across clinical tasks while accounting for disparities among modalities and tasks.

gap.claim: Existing methods require complete labels for all tasks and do not comprehensively address information disparities among modalities and tasks.

contributions.claim: FlexCare decomposes parallel multitask prediction into a series of asynchronous single-task predictions.
A task-agnostic multimodal information extraction module captures decorrelated representations of intra- and inter-modality patterns.

A task-guided hierarchical multimodal fusion module integrates refined modality-level representations into an individual patient-level representation while accounting for modality and task information disparities.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on multiple tasks using MIMIC-IV, MIMIC-CXR, and MIMIC-NOTE are reported to demonstrate the method's effectiveness.
Further analysis is reported to support the feasibility and potential of the multitask strategy in healthcare.

narrative_sequence.summary: Multimodal EHR data can support holistic assessment and multiple predictive healthcare tasks.
Multitask healthcare methods exploit task correlations, but commonly require complete labels and insufficiently address modality and task information disparities.
FlexCare addresses these issues through asynchronous single-task prediction, task-agnostic multimodal extraction, and task-guided hierarchical fusion.
The authors report effectiveness across multiple tasks and datasets, with further analysis of the multitask strategy.

source_observation.claim: Incomplete labels and incomplete multimodal inputs are presented as central flexibility constraints in multitask healthcare prediction.

interpretation.claim: Prediction systems may benefit from decoupling task execution and accommodating missing supervision or modalities.

application.claim: When designing multimodal multitask systems, consider asynchronous task-specific prediction with modality-aware fusion.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy transfers beyond the reported healthcare datasets and tasks.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact handling of incomplete labels or incomplete modalities.
The abstract does not provide baselines, quantitative results, task definitions, or evaluation details.
